title: India-France relations have reached new heights: PM Modi
author: PTI
content_html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday (September 6, 2026) said India-France relations have reached new heights and this strategic partnership is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of long-standing cultural and political ties.

Addressing virtually the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris, PM Modi hoped that the grand temple in Paris will stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity between both the nations.

“In recent years, relations between India and France have reached new heights. Together with my friend, President (Emmanuel) Macron, both nations are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership,” he said.

The Prime Minister said that from technology, AI, and defence to space and climate action, India and France are moving forward together with new momentum and energy.

“We are also celebrating 2026 as the India-France Year of Innovation. This strategic partnership is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of our long-standing cultural and political ties,” he said.

PM Modi said history bears witness that the sacrifice of Indian soldiers in France remains alive in the hearts of people to this day.

“Language enthusiasts also know the pivotal role French scholars played in popularising Sanskrit. Romain Rolland’s writings on Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and Swami Vivekananda brought our societies closer,” he said.

Furthermore, the Prime Minister said, the spiritual journey of 'The Mother' from Paris to the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Puducherry has inspired countless Indian and French seekers. He said decades ago, Srila Prabhupada Swami also visited France, opening a new chapter in spiritual connections through ISKCON.

"Today, yoga has also become a bridge for people-to-people connections between our nations. Images from the Eiffel Tower on International Yoga Day reflect yoga's immense popularity in France,” he said.

title: Construction on Pallikaranai marshland would destroy its ecosystem: Sowmiya Anbumani
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
PMK floor leader in the Assembly Sowmiya Anbumani on Sunday inspected the ongoing construction at the Pallikaranai marshland, which the party has opposed, since it would “destroy” the marshland ecosystem.

Speaking to reporters, Ms. Sowmiya said the entire ecosystem consisting of fish, trees, aquatic plants would be destroyed. “The Pallikaranai Marshland acts as a floodwater drainage basin by storing water and helping replenish groundwater. Therefore, it is essential to protect this marshland. But contrary to this, the Tamil Nadu government is building a retaining wall, thereby putting residential areas at risk of being submerged in floods,” she said.

She said that there is no need to construct a concrete compound wall to protect the marshland and that a simple fence would be sufficient.

She added: “Is a walkway in the marshland really necessary after borrowing ₹21 crore? If a walkway is required, construct it outside the marshland. There is no need for one inside it. When the flood water arrives, there will be no way for the water to drain out because of the retaining wall. Residential areas in the surrounding neighbourhoods could be inundated with rainwater, causing severe damage. The risk of mosquito-borne infections and other diseases will also increase. Even with the intermittent rains we have been receiving over the past few days, water has already begun accumulating here.”

‘Step up surveillance’

Meanwhile, PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss flagged the need to strengthen police surveillance and intelligence operations, so that crimes such as ATM thefts does not occur in Tamil Nadu.

“In the suburban areas of Chennai alone, ATMs belonging to banks have been broken into and robbed at three locations in the past two weeks, with some of the ATM’s being taken away entirely. With the series of ATM robberies by robbers from north India causing considerable fear among the public, the failure of the police to prevent them is condemnable,” he said.

He added: “On the other hand, the brutal killing of a person named Kannan in Besant Nagar, Chennai, by a gang has also caused fear among the public. Kannan was an office-bearer of the ruling TVK and was reportedly involved in criminal cases, including murder. These incidents show no measures have been taken to prevent murders and robberies in Chennai and its suburban areas.”

title: Raj Thackeray warns cadres against communalism distracting economic problems
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray cautioned his cadre members to stay away from religious conflict that could potentially distract them from economic issues, at a meeting at Thane on September 6.

“The atmosphere is being vitiated, and anger is being created in society by heating up the situation through social media. I have the greatest fear that riots will be created during the upcoming Ganesh festival,” he said.

Speaking to his party office-bearers in Thane, Mr. Thackeray urged citizens to remain alert and avoid falling into traps designed to incite religious conflict to distract the public from pressing socio-economic challenges.

He appealed to citizens from both the Hindu and Muslim communities to remain alert.

Mr. Thackeray also raised questions about the first quarter GDP growth of 7.8%, asking why people were being told to avoid foreign trips and buying gold at a time of robust economic growth. Citing what he described as a government report, the MNS chief claimed that 503 companies had shut down their operations in India between 2021 and 2026.

He further said that Prime Minister Modi’s picture can be in government spaces, but not alongside figures of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Dr. B R Ambedkar and Mahatma Jyotirao Phule.A criminal case was registered against Mr. Raj’s son Amit Thackeray and others, for allegedly removing a photograph of PM Modi at the Government Polytechnic Pune. Mr. Raj Thackeray also raised the issue of linguistic politics, claiming non-Marathi speakers are being manipulated to spark language disputes.

title: High-level committee formed in Maharashtra for transparency in recruitment examinations
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The government of Maharashtra formed a high-level committee to study the existing examination system and suggest necessary reforms to make state government recruitment examinations more transparent, secure, reliable, fair and candidate-oriented, according to a decision by the General Administration Department in this regard.

In a meeting held on 12 August 2026 chaired by the Chief Minister, it was decided to completely review the recruitment examination system in the State. Accordingly, a seven-member committee has been formed under the chairmanship of Additional Chief Secretary (Services) of the General Administration Department, V. Radha. The committee comprises Director General of Police Sadanand Date, Secretary, Electronics, Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence Department Virendra Singh, Divisional Commissioner, Nashik Division Praveen Gedam, former Union Public Service Commission member Air Marshal Ajit Shankarrao Bhosale (retd) and Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Mumbai as members. Dr. N. Ramaswamy, Secretary, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying Development and Fisheries, will be the member secretary of the committee. 

The Committee will visit each Revenue Division in the State and hold discussions and consultations with students, candidates, representatives of educational institutions and other relevant stakeholders. Improvements in the examination system will be suggested taking into account their views and suggestions. If necessary, best practices from other States and examination systems from other countries will also be studied.
